Marathon Petroleum rose 0.89% today to close at $395.93, staying within a volatile range as the refiner battles conflicting signals. Oil prices ticked up to $97.26 per barrel domestically on Friday's news that Saudi Arabia shut down a critical pipeline bypass following Iranian attacks on infrastructure—a geopolitical squeeze that typically boosts refiner margins by making crude harder to access. At the same time, U.S. refineries are running at 97.8% capacity with gasoline and diesel inventories building, which can pressure margins if demand weakens.

The stock's 8.91% gain over two weeks reflects the broader whipsaw in energy markets: oil briefly crossed $100 a barrel earlier in the week on Middle East tensions, but retreated when Trump signaled the Iran conflict could wind down after midterms and oil prices would fall. Refiners like Marathon profit when the spread between crude prices and refined product prices widens, so they tend to benefit from supply disruptions—but lose ground if peace talk rumors resurface and crude retreats sharply.
